title: India celebrates 600th Test with 165-run win | Daily FT
summary:
Thursday, 20 August 2026 00:17
-     - 0

Sa’adi Thawfeeq reporting from Galle

GALLE: India wrapped up the first cricket Test against Sri Lanka by 165 runs, 39 minutes after lunch on the fifth and final day at the Galle International Cricket Stadium yesterday to go one-up in the two-match Test series.

The win was even sweeter for India for it came in their 600th Test match.

The writing was on the wall for Sri Lanka after they lost their first four wickets for 47 runs chasing a tall target of 372 and were eventually bowled out for 206. Manav Suthar, with a classical left-arm spinner’s action despite being the most junior of the three spinners India played in the Test, out bowled the other two – Ravindra Jadeja and Kuldeep Yadav - to finish with ten wickets in the match, which included 6/55 in Sri Lanka’s second innings.

That the match dragged onto the second session was mainly due to a gritty 95-run partnership between Dhananjaya de Silva and Sonal Dinusha. Jadeja, who thought that he had dismissed De Silva early in his innings only to discover that it was a no-ball, found his redemption by dismissing the Lankan captain for 59 (151 balls, 7 fours) to break the threatening partnership.

Niroshan Dickwella who played a plucky knock of 80 in the first innings in his return to Test cricket seemed distracted by Yashashvi Jaiswal’s words (goading him to hit a six that he will take him to play in the IPL) and fell to Prasidh Khrishna for 10. Dinusha fought a lone battle and found support from debutant Kheshara Nuwantha with whom he added 43 for the seventh wicket. But once Suthar ended Dinusha’s fighting innings of 84 of 128 balls (8 fours, 1 six) at 199 there was hardly any resistance coming from the rest of the batters. Suthar picked up four wickets within a span of 10 deliveries which included three in one over to bring a swift end to the Lankan innings and the match.    

India’s biggest positives were their two left-handers – Devdutt Padikkal and Suthar. In his comeback Test, Padikkal batted almost faultlessly in both the innings (167 and 44) to take the Player of the Match award.

From Sri Lanka’s point there were a couple of positives too. The two 25-year-olds - Keshara Nuwantha and Sonal Dinusha. The off-spinner bowled with a lot of spirit after a tough opening day and Dinusha was easily Sri Lanka’s best batter in both the innings with 100 and 84.

Sri Lanka have now gone 11 consecutive Tests without a win against India, including 9 losses. Although India were in a dominant position throughout the Test, a good duel was witnessed between bat and ball over the five days.  

The second Test begins at the SSC grounds on 23 August.

title: India rout Pakistan at Hockey World Cup 2026 to qualify for second round | Daily FT
summary:
Thursday, 20 August 2026 00:08
-     - 2

A 10-man India have staved off Pakistan 5-3 and advanced to the second round of the Hockey World Cup after a crucial encounter for the South Asian neighbours at Wagener Stadium.

The victory on Wednesday for eighth-ranked India keeps them in contention for the semifinals while Pakistan were eliminated from the tournament, which is being held in Amstelveen, the Netherlands.

India captain Harmanpreet Singh led the way when he opened scoring in the fourth minute from a penalty corner before Abhishek doubled their lead in the 10th minute off a pass from Mandeep Singh.

Harmanpreet added one more for India in the 20th minute off a penalty corner before Pakistan’s Hannan Shahid scored off a rebound from the goalkeeper.

Abhishek extended the India lead to 4-1 from a lucky deflection off Pakistan’s stick, but Sufyan Khan’s superb dragflick off a penalty corner narrowed the gap to 4-2 at halftime.

Hardik Singh made it 5-2 with a penalty stroke early in the third quarter, which ended with a three-point lead for India and a green card each for Pakistan’s Zikriya Hayat and India’s Rajinder Singh.

Pakistan rallied to make it 5-3 just as the fourth quarter began when Shahid scored in the 45th minute after Hardik lost possession of the ball in the midfield.

India were unsuccessful with their video review taken by Dilpreet Singh in the 53rd minute. It was tough luck for the men in orange when Aditya Lalage received a yellow card in the 55th minute, ruling him out from the rest of the match.

A 10-man India held off Pakistan for the last few minutes to seal the win and progress to the second round. They sit in second place in Pool D with six points from an earlier 3-1 win against Wales.

title: Top order cost us match – Kirsten | Daily FT
summary:
Thursday, 20 August 2026 00:08
-     - 1

Gary Kirsten

GALLE: Sri Lanka’s Head Coach Gary Kirsten said that the failure of the top order batting in both innings cost Sri Lanka the first Test against India which they lost by 165 runs at Galle yesterday.  

“Where we lost the game was in both innings we lost wickets upfront. You just can’t afford that in Test match cricket, especially when you are chasing a total of 462,” said Kirsten at the post media conference.

Sri Lanka were 90-5 in the first innings and 47-4 in the second innings.

“Winning the toss on these wickets – the options are to bat well in the first innings. We ended up playing our first innings on the third day when the wicket took the most amount of turn. On day four and five it played a little bit easier and the ball got softer much quicker,” said Kirsten.

“It was a very good Test match wicket. To give away 178 runs in the first innings that’s where it cost us the game, we didn’t bat all that well apart from a great partnership of 146 between (Sonal) Dinusha and (Niroshan) Dickwella. The pitch played really well and didn’t turn hugely throughout the game. It was a good cricket wicket.”         

Kirsten said that there were some positives Sri Lanka could take out of the match.

“From being 99-5 at the beginning of the third day and taking the Test match into the afternoon of the fifth day was particularly pleasing and the fight. We were keen to try and stay in the Test match. We still believed even this morning we could work something up to win the Test or certainly draw it. Very pleased with the energy and attitude of the team around that.”

Kirsten was full of praise for Sonal Dinusha and debutant Keshara Nuwantha.

“This is his (Dinusha’s) fourth Test match, to see the way he’s played is very exciting for Sri Lankan cricket. His love for Test cricket and playing the way and that style is particularly pleasing to me to watch. We certainly would encourage our players to have that Test match mindset and attitude,” said Kirsten.

“The challenge for the modern players especially in Sri Lanka is that we don’t play many Test matches. We have at least six lined up in the next six months or so. It’s great to get into the Test match game a little bit and then try to score runs and bat for a long period of time and have an influence on the game. Sonal has done that a few times in the West Indies as well, where under pressure he was able to make performances. He’s got good mental strength, courage and resilience and he is a good example for all other players. That step up you’ve got to be on your game mentally to manage it.”

“I was very impressed with Keshara Nuwantha. On his debut he bowled exceptionally well. He got four wickets in the Test match and he batted for 70 balls in the second innings. Our conversation with all the lower order batters is to bat as many balls as they can in these conditions. He showed real grit and determination.” (ST)

title: Sri Lanka without three top batters for second Test | Daily FT
summary:
Thursday, 20 August 2026 00:07
-     - 2

Sri Lanka will be without Dinesh Chandimal for the second Test against India starting at the SSC grounds on 23 August.

Chandimal was concussed and replaced by Pasindu Sooriyabandara as concussion sub on the fourth day of the first Test at Galle after he hit his shoulder and head hard on the ground while fielding.

Prior to that wicket-keeper/batsman Kusal Mendis was ruled out of the series with a hamstring injury and Pathum Nissanka who missed the first Test after undergoing surgery to his wrist has also been ruled out of the second Test.

“We are missing a few guys, but it creates an opportunity for young players to come in and put their hands up. Players who have got good first class records in this country,” said head coach Gary Kirsten.

“It’s unfortunate we lost Dinesh (Chandimal). He is a quality Test match veteran. In this circumstance he would have been a really important player for us. That was unfortunate but that’s the nature of the game. It’s nice that a few guys who have played a handful of Test matches are getting a chance to bat in the top order and understand what it is like to play Test cricket against some of the best Test cricket nations in the world.” (ST)

title: Sabalenka cruises through as Medvedev falls to Nakashima at Cincinnati Open | Daily FT
summary:
Thursday, 20 August 2026 00:06
-     - 1

Sabalenka

World number one Aryna Sabalenka dominated China’s Wang Xinyu 6-1, 6-3 to cruise into the Cincinnati Masters fourth round, while Daniil Medvedev suffered a shock defeat to Brandon Nakashima.

Sabalenka took only 20 minutes on Tuesday to breeze through the first set against her 36th-ranked opponent and began the second set with a break of serve.

She kept up the pressure in the second set, with Wang double-faulting on the top seed’s first match point after 54 minutes.

The victory marked the 45th in a row for Sabalenka at the Masters 1000 level.

“I cannot complain. She’s a tough opponent,” Sabalenka said. “To win in straight sets like this in under an hour is insane.

“I’m super happy to be through. I really trusted myself and went for my shots. I wasn’t overthinking. I was able to stay focused and be in every point.”

Sabalenka next plays Czech Sara Bejlek, a 4-6, 6-1, 6-2 winner over Ekaterina Alexandrova.

Fourth seed Coco Gauff needed to battle after a sizzling first set in a 6-1, 7-6 (7/3) victory over fellow American Ann Li.

The 2023 champion had it all her own way in the opening set against her 29th-ranked foe, winning in 30 minutes. The pair exchanged early breaks in the second on the way to a tie-breaker, in which Gauff seized a 4-1 lead and won on her third match point.

“She played better in the second set, and I missed a couple of break opportunities,” Gauff said. “I tried to forget about those.

“It was hard to control the ball for both of us, and it was my first time playing a day match on this centre court, so I had to adjust to that.”

Mirra Andreeva’s French Open reigning champion status counted for little as the fifth seed struggled to close out a 6-1, 7-6 (7/5) victory over Janice Tjen.

The Indonesian challenger, ranked 37, was bowled over in the first set but made Andreeva work to finally advance.

“In the first, I was in command, and she had unforced errors here and there, but in the second, after a couple of games, I started getting nervous. She made fewer mistakes – it turned into a match of mentality and physicality,” Andreeva said.

Eighth seed Elina Svitolina was forced to withdraw before her match against Wang Xiyu with an ankle injury.

“I’ve been advised by the doctors to take a little bit of time to rest and recover completely,” the Ukrainian said in a statement.

Canada’s second-seeded Felix Auger-Aliassime eliminated Argentina’s Juan Manuel Cerundolo 7-5, 6-1 in 90 minutes.

“It was a tricky start, finding my rhythm,” the Canadian said. “Lefties are tricky, you don’t play them so often. You can prepare all you want, but until you step onto the court you can’t find your right adjustments. Then you feel comfortable.”

Washington winner and fifth seed Taylor Fritz fired eight aces in defeating Daniel Merida 6-3, 6-4 in 83 minutes. The Spaniard made 25 unforced errors as Fritz booked a fourth-round match against Australian Chris O’Connell, who is 0-3 against the American.

Sri Lanka Netball needs reform: Time to open doors to professional governance | Daily FT
summary:
Thursday, 20 August 2026 00:04
-     - 2

By Hishan Welmilla 

Sri Lanka’s disappointing campaign at the 14th Asian Netball Championship in Hong Kong should be treated as far more than a failure on the court. Finishing third and missing the opportunity to qualify for the Netball World Cup after 21 years represents a significant setback for a country that has traditionally been one of Asia’s leading netball nations.

The defeat should therefore trigger a serious examination of how the sport is administered, rather than simply placing the blame on the players or coaching staff.

Sri Lanka has talented players capable of competing at the highest level in Asia. However, talent alone cannot sustain international success. A modern sporting organisation requires professional administration, strategic planning, financial discipline, high-performance structures and strong leadership. The recent setbacks suggest that Sri Lanka Netball must now consider whether its existing governance structure is capable of delivering those requirements.

One important area that deserves urgent attention is the constitution governing Sri Lanka Netball. The current structure, which effectively restricts the governing body to women, should be reconsidered in the interests of professionalism and good governance.

This is not an argument against women’s leadership. Women have played, coached and administered Sri Lankan netball with tremendous dedication, and their contribution must continue to be respected. The issue is whether leadership positions should be determined by gender rather than competence, experience, professional qualifications and the ability to deliver results.

Sport has changed dramatically. Netball is no longer simply an amateur game administered through traditional structures. It is an international sporting industry involving sponsorship, broadcasting, athlete welfare, sports science, marketing, digital media, commercial partnerships and high-performance programs.

Sri Lanka therefore needs to examine successful international models. Singapore provides an example of a more professionally structured approach, where administrative and executive responsibilities are separated from the traditional representation of the sport. Sri Lanka should study such models and identify what can be adapted to its own circumstances.

One proposal that deserves serious consideration is the appointment of a professional Chief Executive Officer to manage the day-to-day affairs of Sri Lanka Netball. Such a position should be open to both men and women and should be filled through a transparent, merit-based recruitment process.

The CEO should not replace the elected governing body. Instead, the position should strengthen it by bringing professional management into the organisation. The elected officials can provide policy direction and represent the interests of the sport, while a professionally appointed CEO can be held accountable for implementing strategy, managing finances, developing commercial opportunities, coordinating national teams and establishing long-term development programs.

The writer has previously advocated the appointment of a professional male CEO following the 2018 World Cup, believing that introducing professional executive management could provide a fresh direction for the sport. This was again brought in 2025; 

https://www.ft.lk/Sports/The-future-of-netball-in-Sri-Lanka/23-682720

https://www.ft.lk/sports/Sri-Lanka-Netball-at-crossroads-Navigating-crisis-and-seeking-revival/23-779301.

However, given the latest setback, there is a strong argument for beginning the reform process much earlier rather than waiting until another major tournament exposes the same weaknesses.

The Sports Ministry must therefore take the lead in initiating a comprehensive review of the Sri Lanka Netball constitution. Any amendments should be developed through consultation with former players, coaches, administrators, athletes, clubs, provincial associations, legal experts and sports-management professionals.

The objective should not be to remove women from the administration of netball. Quite the opposite: the objective should be to create a system where the best people—regardless of gender—can contribute their expertise.

Sri Lanka cannot afford another cycle of disappointment followed by temporary changes. The missed World Cup opportunity should become a turning point.

The Sports Minister now has an opportunity to modernise the governance of Sri Lankan netball, introduce professional executive management and establish clear accountability.

The players deserve nothing less. Sri Lankan netball deserves nothing less. And the millions of supporters who have stood behind the national team for decades deserve an administration capable of building a stronger future.

The time has come to change the constitution, professionalise the administration and give Sri Lankan netball the leadership structure it needs to return to the world stage.

title: Hameedia ties up with NOC SL and CGA SL as Team Sri Lanka’s Official Clothing Partner for upcoming international sporting events | Daily FT
summary:
Thursday, 20 August 2026 00:03
-     - 2

Hameedia Head of Design and Business Development Mikail Hameed (left) exchanges the MoU with National Olympic Committee of Sri Lanka (NOCSL) Chairman Asanga Seneviratne

Hameedia has been appointed the Official Clothing Partner for Team Sri Lanka, following the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the National Olympic Committee of Sri Lanka (NOC) and the Commonwealth Games Association (CGA) of Sri Lanka. The signing ceremony was held on 11 August 2026 at Olympic House, formalising a partnership that will see Hameedia dress Team Sri Lanka’s athletes and officials at upcoming international sporting events.

The agreement was signed on behalf of Hameedia by, Head of Design and Business Development Mikail Hameed, together with the management board of the National Olympic Committee. The signing ceremony was also attended by Marketing and Business Development – Hameedia Women Habiba Hameed, Husn Brand Manager Asma Hussain, and Hameedia Head of Marketing Kasun Weerasinghe. Representing the NOC SL and CGA SL were NOC/CGA Sri Lanka President Asanga Seneviratne, NOC/CGA Sri Lanka Secretary General Rifdy Fahmy, NOC Sri Lanka Chairman of Marketing and Sponsorship Committee Dilshan Mohamed, Team Sri Lanka for the 7th Asian Indoor and Martial Arts Games Riyadh 2026 Chef de Mission Danuna Tilakaratne, and NOC Sri Lanka Games Committee and Athletes Commission Chairman Niluka Karunaratne OLY.

Under the partnership, Hameedia will design and produce official team apparel for Team Sri Lanka, beginning with the Asian Indoor and Martial Arts Games 2026 and continuing through the Commonwealth Youth Games 2027.

Hameedia Head of Design and Business Development Mikail Hameed said, “Being named the Official Clothing Partner for Team Sri Lanka is a proud moment for us. It reflects the trust placed in Hameedia’s craftsmanship and design capability, and we look forward to bringing that same standard of quality and pride to our athletes as they represent the country on the international stage.”

This partnership marks a significant milestone for Hameedia, extending the brand’s presence beyond retail and tailoring into national sporting representation. Hameedia will continue to work closely with the National Olympic Committee in the lead-up to each event, ensuring Team Sri Lanka is outfitted with apparel that reflects both national pride and Hameedia’s legacy of quality craftsmanship.

With this partnership, Hameedia reaffirms its commitment to supporting Sri Lankan talent on the global stage, further strengthening its position as a brand synonymous with heritage, craftsmanship, and national pride. For more information, visit www.hameedia.com or follow Hameedia on social media.

title: JXG partners Mercantile Hockey Association as Title Sponsor of Corporate Hockey Tournaments | Daily FT
summary:
Thursday, 20 August 2026 00:02
-     - 2

Title sponsorship cheque handover to the Mercantile Hockey Association for its 9-A-Side and 7-A-Side Hockey Tournaments, with JXG Founder and Chairman Emeritus C.T.A. Schaffter, joined by officials from JXG and the Association

JXG (Janashakthi Group) has partnered with the Mercantile Hockey Association as the Title Sponsor of the 9-A-Side and 7-A-Side Hockey Tournaments for a three-year period from 2026 to 2028, continuing a longstanding connection to the sport that first began with the Group’s Founder and Chairman Emeritus C.T.A. Schaffter.

C.T.A. Schaffter’s association with hockey spans over 25 years, beginning during his school days and extending to the national level. He represented the Mercantile Hockey Association at the National Championships for several years and was part of the Mercantile side that secured the Senior National Hockey Championships of Ceylon on seven occasions, in 1956, 1958, 1959, 1960, 1961, 1962 and 1963. In 1957, he captained the Colombo Hockey Association to victory at the Senior National Hockey Championships of Ceylon.

His contributions to the sport extend well beyond his playing career. C.T.A. Schaffter served as a National Selector in Hockey from 1960 to 1962 and again in 1966, when he was appointed Chairman of Selectors. He returned to the National Selection Committee from 1972 to 1973 and continued until his resignation in 1974. He also served as Vice President of the Mercantile Hockey Association from 1968 to 1971 and as Vice Patron from 1972 to 1976. His leadership in the sport further expanded to the Ceylon/Sri Lanka Hockey Federation, where he served in multiple senior capacities including Vice Patron, Vice President, and Secretary, in addition to serving as Manager of the Sri Lanka National Hockey Team.

The sponsorship cheque was officially handed over in the presence of C.T.A. Schaffter, Founder and Chairman Emeritus of JXG, together with officials of JXG and the Mercantile Hockey Association.

The partnership carries forward a relationship with hockey that has been closely associated with C.T.A. Schaffter for decades, while providing a platform for JXG to support the continued development of corporate hockey in Sri Lanka. Through the 9-A-Side and 7-A-Side tournaments, the sponsorship will contribute towards creating greater opportunities for corporate players, recognising sporting talent, and strengthening the role of hockey within Sri Lanka’s business community.

The partnership also reflects JXG’s commitment to carrying forward the sporting values and legacy that have been part of its history, while supporting initiatives that unite talent, competition, and camaraderie across the corporate sector.

title: Under 14 Rugby Tens to lighten Central Province | Daily FT
summary:

By Shamseer Jaleel

The All Island Under-14 Ten-a-Side Rugby Tournament will bring together Sri Lanka’s finest junior rugby talent for a two-day battle on 21 and 22 August in the Central Hills.

This year’s event will feature 32 teams representing schools from across the island, with the young players competing for junior supremacy.

Day One will see Groups A to D in action at the Trinity College Rugby Ground, Pallekelle, while Groups E to H will compete at the Digana Public Ground. The tournament will move to the Trinity College Rugby Stadium in Pallekelle on the second day, where the knockout stages will be worked off.

Zahira College, the defending champions, will enter the tournament with confidence after edging Wesley College 5-0 in last year’s final. They will face a strong challenge from several leading rugby schools hoping to make their mark at junior level.
